head: 51767bd8a65b7916bec5c58daed9305eb5083b92
claim: A device can be let into an existing Boat computer over plain SSH: boat().sshAccess adds one key and returns the target and host key to pin

steps.start: Built SDK in the worktree (dist present). A fake Boat sandbox server (loopback, startFakeSandboxServer) running with one existing computer created through boat().create. No real key, account or spend.
steps: Started a fake Boat server on loopback and created an existing computer named existing-box through the boat() adapter.
Called sshAccess on that computer with one OpenSSH ed25519 public key line.
Read the returned target: host, port, user and the SHA256 fingerprint of the host key to pin.
Checked the public key was added to that computer on the server.
Called sshAccess again with the text 'not a key' and read the typed error and message.
Checked that the refused input added no second key, then closed the server.
steps.result: The output text shows sshAccess returning host 127.0.0.1, port 22, user 'user' and host key fingerprint SHA256:gNSIRW+2Iyiuvsdp/bgjy38bvWHw6wQm3tuoXrl3WjQ; the one ssh-ed25519 key is listed on the computer; a malformed key fails with code 'bad-recipe' and message 'publicKey: must be one OpenSSH public key line' and leaves the key list unchanged.

verdicts.seen: I read the whole capture: 1 target record, 1 sshAccess-target, 1 keys-added entry, and 1 keys-after-refusal entry. sshAccess-target returns host 127.0.0.1, port 22, user "user", and fingerprint SHA256:gNSIRW+2Iyiuvsdp/bgjy38bvWHw6wQm3tuoXrl3WjQ, which covers returning the host key to pin. keys-added-to-computer holds exactly one ed25519 key labeled "phone", which covers adding one key. The bad-key case returns code "bad-recipe" with a publicKey format error, and keys-after-refusal still holds only that one key, so the refusal left nothing extra. The outcome names one part, so parts is empty.
